findings.title: Delete-cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. It does not invalidate or refetch viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation. Since SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper displays cache status from that query and may not provide an onChanged handler that invalidates it, the UI can keep showing the old cache status and timestamp after cache deletion succeeds.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the maximum updatedAt for CalendarCache rows without filtering by expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only treats rows with expiresAt >= now as valid. As a result, connectedCalendars can report cacheUpdatedAt and show cache actions for credentials whose cache entries are expired, misleading users about whether valid cached data exists.

findings.title: Disabled scope is not propagated to credential actions
findings.body: The wrapper computes shouldDisableConnectionModification as isDisabled || disableConnectionModification, but ConnectedCalendarList receives only disableConnectionModification. When disabledScope matches the current scope, calendar switches are disabled, but CredentialActionsDropdown can still allow deleting cache or disconnecting the integration, defeating the disabled-scope restriction.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The cache last-updated timestamp is formatted using Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') regardless of the user's locale. This ignores localized date preferences and can show an English/US-formatted timestamp to non-English users.

findings.title: Empty actions container is rendered when dropdown is hidden
findings.body: The actions prop always renders a fixed-width div around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for delegation credentials with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, the empty container remains and creates unnecessary blank space in the list item or alert action area.

findings.title: Authorization failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the current user. This will be surfaced/logged as an internal server error rather than an explicit tRPC FORBIDDEN or NOT_FOUND error, making client error handling and observability less accurate.

findings.title: Webhook helper script uses macOS-only sed and fragile relative env path
findings.body: The script uses sed -i '' which is BSD/macOS syntax and will fail on GNU/Linux. It also writes to ../.env relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running it from the repository root or another directory can modify the wrong file or create an unexpected .env file.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without declaring tsx
findings.body: The dev:cron script was changed to npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not listed as a devDependency. npx may download or prompt to install tsx at runtime, making the script network-dependent and less reproducible across environments.

findings.title: No automated tests for cache deletion authorization/status
findings.body: There are no automated tests for the new deleteCache handler's ownership check, the cache deletion behavior, or the connectedCalendars cache-status enrichment. These paths affect authorization and user-visible data, and regressions could go unnoticed without coverage.
